newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees shopping mall boom ahead.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees shopping mall boom ahead.

text.p: Total floorspace of Hungary's large shopping centres will rise sixfold to 1.0-1.5 million square metres by 2000, the industry and trade ministry's publication forecast on Wednesday.

Gyorgy Vamos, General Secretary of the National Trade Alliance, wrote in the monthly Ipari Szemle that new shopping malls were transforming the retail sector fundamentally, although reaching western standards would take several years.
Four malls and supermarkets built recently have added 150,000 square metres to the 100,000 square metre total floorspace of shopping centres, with another 400,000 square metres under construction.

Western-style supermarkets and department stores with a large diversity of goods and relatively low transport and sales costs are increasingly popular and are likely to boost their market share to 10-15 percent by 2000 from a few percent, Vamos said.

This would still be well short of the 70-80 percent of total sales these outlets usually represent in western European countries as consumer spending would recover slowly from the fall by over 25 percent in retail turnover between 1990 and 1996, he added.
Hungarian towns also need time for the infrastructural developments essential for the operation of large centres, he added.
However, after 2000, Hungary will still remain a large market for shopping centre constructors, he said.
He added that in 1996 investments in Hungary's retail sector rose by more than 50 percent to 70 billion forints.
